objective.stem: A digital device is a machine that works with ___
objective.answer: electricity and shows things on a screen
distractors: fire and shows things on a wall
water and keeps things in a pot
rope and pulls things up a hill

objective.stem: This one is NOT a digital device ___
The device used for taking pictures is a ___
A tablet is different from a desktop because it is ___
objective.answer: flat, light and touched with the finger
distractors: big, heavy and fixed on a table
made of wood and of cloth

objective.stem: A computer is big and has a screen, keys and a ___
A machine that opens and shuts like a book, with a battery, is a ___
The smallest and lightest computer to carry is the ___
The part that shows pictures, letters and numbers is the ___
We press keys to put information into the computer with the ___
The part held in the hand that moves the arrow on the screen is the ___
The machine that puts the picture or letter out on paper is a ___
A computer in the bank is used to ___
objective.answer: count money and print a receipt
distractors: sweep the floor of the hall

objective.stem: The price of goods in a shop is read by a ___
Time on a device should be shared between learning and ___
objective.answer: play, with a limit on play

objective.stem: Water inside a device ___
A laptop should be carried ___
objective.answer: closed in two hands inside a padded bag
distractors: open in only one small hand
by its long wire, dragged along

objective.stem: The cable is taken out of the socket by holding ___
Before we switch off, we save the work and ___
objective.answer: shut the programme, then kill the power
distractors: pull the cable out in a hurry
shake the monitor once or twice

objective.stem: The room in the school where many computers are kept is the ___
In the lab we move about by ___
If a machine gives smoke or a bad smell, we ___
objective.answer: leave it and tell the teacher at once
distractors: pour cold water on the machine
press every key on the keyboard

objective.stem: Long ago, people counted with stones and with a frame of sliding beads called a(n) ___
The first machines used parts that glowed and grew hot called ___
The tiny part that replaced the hot vacuum tube was the ___
Computers became ___
The machine built by Babbage to work out tables of numbers without mistakes was the ___
Babbage's plans could not be built fully because the ___
objective.answer: workshop of his day could not make such parts
distractors: the money he had for the metal parts
the plans he drew on his paper only
the numbers he wrote in his log book

objective.stem: A set of written instructions for a machine is called a ___
A computer language was named after ___
"A device is a servant, not a ___

subobjective.stem: Mention five digital devices you know.
State three things a smartphone does.
Name the four basic parts of a computer.
Say what each of these is used for: monitor and CPU.
Mention three places where a computer is used.
Give four rules for caring for a device.
points: wipe with a soft dry cloth
do not drop or hit it

subobjective.stem: State three safety rules of the computer lab.
points: no food or drink on the desk
do not touch cables or sockets

subobjective.stem: Name the three kinds of computer we learnt.
Mention three uses of the abacus or old counting things.
Say two things about Babbage and Ada Lovelace.
points: Babbage designed the Analytical Engine and the Difference Engine

theory.stem: Explain what technology means and give four devices at home that are digital
Describe how you care for a tablet or a laptop, in four points
